purpose: Provide deterministic translation-only min/max limits on one caller-selected fixed world-space direction projection while preserving slack motion inside the interval and free perpendicular translation, including one-step shared composer/activity/isolation integration.

properties.limits: bounded explicit fixed world-space directions with minOffset and/or maxOffset
properties.options: bounded pre/post position and velocity iteration counts

limitations: slack motion inside the allowed interval is intentionally free
direction does not rotate with bodies
not a full prismatic or slider joint
no angular inertia, rotating anchors, angular limits or motors
the standalone step entrypoint still performs its own donor-core step; mixed-family callers must use the shared composer/activity/isolation path to preserve the one-step contract
component isolation is topology-wide even while a direction-limit interval is physically slack
post-core projection can change positions after donor contact evidence was produced

proves: normalized fixed-direction one-sided and ranged limits
slack motion inside the projected interval
direction limits are the seventh deterministic composer family around exactly one donor-core step
disabled direction limits are excluded by the activity gate
enabled direction-limit edges can join component isolation even while slack
caller collision groups are restored after the donor collision stage

truth.basis: The capability remains explicitly a fixed world-space projected translation range primitive and is not relabeled as a rotating prismatic joint; slack topology and physical correction are kept distinct.

agency.basis: Callers choose direction, min/max bounds, activity state, isolation request and bounded solver factors/iterations.

continuity.basis: The donor core remains byte-for-byte preserved while existing direction-limit primitives are reused inside the shared one-step stack.

wisdom-before-speed.basis: Shared integration calls the existing prepare/measure primitives around one donor-core step rather than chaining standalone wrappers and risking a second integration.
